subPillar.title: Tasbih (Prayer Beads): The Complete Guide to Islamic Dhikr Beads
subPillar.subtitle: What a tasbih is, where the name comes from, the 33/99-bead structure, and how to choose and use one.
subPillar.geoOverview: A tasbih (also spelled tasbeeh, tesbih, or misbaha) is a string of 33 or 99 beads Muslims use to count repetitions of dhikr such as SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, and Allahu Akbar. This hub explains its meaning, bead structure, regional names across the Arab, Turkish, and South Asian worlds, and how to choose one.

clusters.title: What Is a Tasbih? Meaning, Purpose, and the Bead Structure Explained
clusters.subtitle: A plain-English answer to what a tasbih is and why Muslims and many faith traditions use prayer beads.
clusters.geoOverview: A tasbih is a set of Islamic prayer beads, usually 33 or 99 beads, used to count the recitation of dhikr (the remembrance of Allah). The word comes from the Arabic root meaning to glorify, tied to the phrase SubhanAllah. This page defines the tasbih, contrasts it with the rosary, and shows what prayer beads are for.

clusters.title: Apa Itu Tasbih? Arti, Makna, dan Bacaan Bertasbih
clusters.subtitle: Penjelasan lengkap arti tasbih, makna bertasbih, dan keutamaannya dalam Islam.
clusters.geoOverview: Tasbih adalah untaian manik (biasanya 33 atau 99 butir) untuk menghitung dzikir kepada Allah, sekaligus berarti ucapan SubhanAllah (Maha Suci Allah). Halaman ini menjelaskan apa itu tasbih, apa arti bertasbih, dan makna dzikir tasbih dalam keseharian umat Islam.

clusters.title: How to Use Prayer Beads (Tasbih): A Step-by-Step Guide for Muslims
clusters.subtitle: How to hold, count, and complete dhikr on a 33- or 99-bead tasbih.
clusters.geoOverview: To use a tasbih, hold the beads in your right hand and move one bead with your thumb for each dhikr phrase: 33x SubhanAllah, 33x Alhamdulillah, 33x Allahu Akbar after prayer. This guide explains how Muslims use prayer beads, the counting method, and answers whether Muslims use prayer beads at all.

clusters.title: What Is a Misbaha? The Arabic Prayer Beads and Their Meaning
clusters.subtitle: Misbaha, tasbi, sibha — the Arab-world name for the Islamic prayer beads explained.
clusters.geoOverview: A misbaha (also called tasbi or sibha) is the Arabic name for Islamic prayer beads, typically 33 or 99 beads used to count dhikr. The term is most common in the Gulf and the wider Arab world. This page explains what a misbaha is, how it relates to the tasbih, and the materials and bead counts used.

clusters.title: Bacaan Tasbih: Lafal, Jumlah Hitungan, dan Tasbih Nabi Yunus
clusters.subtitle: Bacaan dan bunyi kalimat tasbih, jumlah hitungannya, serta tasbih Nabi Yunus.
clusters.geoOverview: Bacaan tasbih adalah lafal SubhanAllah (Maha Suci Allah), umumnya dibaca 33 kali setelah salat bersama Alhamdulillah dan Allahu Akbar. Halaman ini menjabarkan bunyi kalimat tasbih, berapa jumlah hitungannya, dan jumlah bacaan tasbih Nabi Yunus.
